commands.name: agent
commands.summary: print this capability map (read once, then drive)

commands.name: status
commands.summary: what is built / signed / published, and where

commands.name: auth
commands.summary: save a credential (e.g. fury token) to the OS keychain

commands.name: secrets
commands.summary: the credentials and tools your channels need, and how to set them up for CI
notes: wharfy reads every credential from the environment, so the same commands run on a laptop and in a GitHub Actions workflow
the token GitHub Actions hands a workflow can only write to that repository: channels that write elsewhere (tap, bucket, gated forks) need a PAT registered as a secret

commands.name: init
commands.summary: tell agents to release via wharfy (writes AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md)

commands.name: build
notes: the Go build path shells out to goreleaser, so it must be on PATH — on a CI runner install it explicitly (wharfy secrets lists the tools your config needs); BYO inputs (prebuilt: / bundle:) never call it

commands.name: sign
commands.summary: codesign macOS binaries with your identity (opt-in; skipped if none)

commands.name: release
commands.summary: upload the github release (archives, packages, install.sh, install.ps1, latest.json)
notes: re-running it on the same tag is safe: the release is reused and assets already there are replaced, so a workflow that failed at publish can simply be re-run

when the repo you are releasing is wharfy itself, artifacts are generated by the running binary: build it from HEAD first (go build -o /tmp/wharfy ./cmd/wharfy), or --yes is refused (override: --allow-stale-generator)

commands.name: publish
commands.summary: push to owned channels; prepare gated ones
notes: when the repo you are releasing is wharfy itself, artifacts are generated by the running binary: build it from HEAD first (go build -o /tmp/wharfy ./cmd/wharfy), or --yes is refused (override: --allow-stale-generator)

commands.name: verify
commands.summary: check each channel from the consumer side (--install: install from it and run it)

commands.name: version
commands.summary: print wharfy's own version (not your project's)

channels.name: script
notes: on failure the scripts print the cause and the next move; they never retry, never fall back to a mirror, and never elevate

install.sh / install.ps1 exit codes: 0=installed; 1=unexpected failure — unclassified, please report; 2=unsupported platform (os/arch); 3=download failed (dns / tls / proxy / http error / missing asset); 4=cannot write to the install prefix (permission, read-only fs, no space)
